newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Norilsk unit to shed 10,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Russia Norilsk unit to shed 10,000 jobs.

text.p: The main unit of Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group plans to shed 10,000 jobs this year, slimming its total workforce by 8.3 percent as part of a restructuring plan, a senior company official said on Thursday.
Oleg Budargin, deputy director of the Norilsk Mining and Metallurgical Complex, told Reuters that around 10,000 workers who had applied to leave their jobs would be let go this year and not replaced.

Some of the employees are in the mining, metal enriching and processing sectors, he said. A senior trade union official said that the cuts would cost Norilsk seven trillion roubles in various benefits, and that non-payment of the benefits could go against the spirit of a recent agreement with management on labour disputes.

"These people have said that they want to go of their own free will, but it will cost seven trillion roubles to resettle them and to pay the various benefits to which they are entitled," said Boris Degtyaryov, deputy chairman of Norilsk's United Trade Union Committee.

"It could cause a problem with a protocol if the obligations are not met," he said, referring to an agreement signed between management and labour in March in which workers, upset over wage and other arrears, agreed not to disrupt output before July 1.

The main plant is owned by RAO Norilsky Nikel 0#NKEL.RUO, one of the world's most important non-ferrous and precious metals producers. The Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex has 120,000 employees, including 15,000 miners, 20,000 metallurgists and 15,000 metal enrichers. The remaining 70,000 are in auxiliary jobs.
